newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish poll approves tighter bail law.
newsitem.headline: Irish poll approves tighter bail law.

text.p: Irish voters, worried about a crime wave, have overwhelmingly approved a change to the constitution to tighten laws governing bail, according to partial results of a referendum released on Friday.

They showed that voters endorsed by a 3-1 majority a proposal to allow courts to refuse bail to anyone charged with a serious crime if police believed the suspect might commit another offence while awaiting trial.
But turnout in the referendum, which was held on Wednesday, was a disappointing 35 per cent overall, some 20 percent less than the average for such votes.
The government, opposition and police all backed plans to make it harder for suspects to be awarded bail as part of a drive to stamp out crime, especially drug-related offences.

Worries about the growing use of drugs reached fever point in June when the country's top investigative journalist, Veronica Guerin, was murdered by a suspected contract killer believed to have been hired by a gangland drug lord.
Official figures show that the number of offences committed by bailed suspects has doubled to more than 5,000 over the past decade.
But civil liberties groups fear that the change will effectively make suspects guilty before they are proved innocent and infringe their civil rights.
They have also predicted that jailed criminals will have to be freed early to make space for people refused bail, putting the public at risk.
